cards.explanation: The answer is that Peter follows Jesus at a distance. Peter, one of Jesus' twelve disciples, follows all the way to the high priest's courtyard (Matthew 26:58). The rest of the disciples had already deserted Jesus and fled (Matthew 26:56), so Peter is doing something different here. I think he's trying to stay close and stay careful at the same time. Not easy to do, friends.

The answer is guards. Peter goes in and sits down with the guards (Matthew 26:58). Sitting down next to them takes some nerve, friends. I'd have picked a seat by the exit, and then maybe a seat outside.

The answer is the temple of God. The two witnesses say Jesus claimed, "I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days." (Matthew 26:61) Many false witnesses came forward before them, but the council did not find the false testimony it was seeking (Matthew 26:60). Then these two come forward and declare it. It's the temple of God they bring up, friends.

The answer is that Jesus remains silent. The high priest asks, "Have You no answer?" (Matthew 26:62), and Jesus remains silent (Matthew 26:63). The text doesn't tell us why, so I won't guess. What it does tell us is that He said nothing to those charges. Just quiet in the middle of all that noise.

The answer is whether He is the Christ. The high priest says, "I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God." (Matthew 26:63) That's a direct question put to Jesus under oath. The charges about the temple don't get the final word here. This question does.

The answer is blasphemed. The high priest tears his clothes and declares, "He has blasphemed!" (Matthew 26:65) Jesus had just told them they would see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power (Matthew 26:64). That's what comes right before the high priest says it. Blasphemy is the charge he makes.

The answer is that they have all heard it themselves. The high priest says, "Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy." (Matthew 26:65) His point is that everyone in the room just heard Jesus' words with their own ears. Earlier the council had been seeking false testimony (Matthew 26:59). Now the high priest says they need no more witnesses.

The answer is True. The high priest asks, "What do you think?" and the council answers, "He deserves to die…" (Matthew 26:66) Back in verse 59, the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony in order to put Him to death. I think this is a heavy moment, friends.

The answer is that he says he doesn't know what she's talking about. The servant girl says, "You also were with Jesus the Galilean…" and Peter denies it before them all: "I do not know what you are talking about." (Matthew 26:69-70) I think this is a rough moment for Peter, since he followed Jesus all the way to this courtyard (Matthew 26:58). It's the first of the denials.

The answer is True. When Peter has gone out to the gateway, another servant girl sees him and tells the people there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth." (Matthew 26:71) Different girl, different spot. Peter changed locations, and the same claim followed him.

The answer is that he swears an oath. Matthew 26:72 says Peter denied it again with an oath, saying, "I do not know the man!" That's the second denial, and it's stronger than the first one. In verse 70, he only said he didn't know what she meant. Now he's put an oath behind it.

The answer is accent. The people standing nearby say, "Surely you are one of them, for your accent gives you away." (Matthew 26:73) The first two times it was servant girls, and this time it's a group standing close. That's more people talking to one man.

The answer is that he begins to curse and swear. Matthew 26:74 says Peter began to curse and swear to them, and he says, "I do not know the man!" The first denial was words, the second an oath, and now this. And right then a rooster crowed. Peter is in deep, friends.

The answer is three. Peter remembers the word Jesus had spoken: "Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." (Matthew 26:75) Count them up with me: the servant girl, the second servant girl, and the people standing nearby. That makes three. Jesus' word held true down to the number.

The answer is False. The text says Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken, and then he "…went outside and wept bitterly." (Matthew 26:75) He doesn't go back inside. He steps away from the courtyard and cries. I think that's a man whose heart just hit the floor.
